info.title: Superbot API
info.description: Call models through one OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible gateway, and manage the account behind it: scoped caller keys, custom endpoints, usage and spend, teams and devices. Errors share one envelope (`error`, `message`, `doc_url`, `request_id`); lists page with `limit`, `after_id` and `before_id`.

tags.name: Usage & spend

tier.description: `link`: terminal and relay only. `data`: link plus the synced data the linking app granted.

state.description: `online`: polling now. `asleep`: suspended by its vendor (jobs wait `queued_asleep`). `offline`: not seen recently.

expires_at.description: The next lifecycle deadline (ISO 8601), the one `expiry_kind` names. Warned 3 days ahead.

expiry_kind.description: `data_idle`: 14 days idle drops the data tier to link. `reconfirm`: the 90-day re-confirm is due (missed: link tier). `link_idle`: 30 days idle unlinks it.

reconfirm_due_at.description: When the data tier must be re-confirmed (POST /me/devices/{device_id}/agent-reconfirm); null at the link tier.

AgentDeviceFacet.description: Present only on a Device of kind `agent_computer`.

args.description: The Helper tool's own args, camelCase, per kind: bash {command, cwd?, timeoutMs?, runInBackground?, interactive?} (interactive: a real tty, answered with bash_write; open a terminal pane with {command: <login shell>, runInBackground: true, interactive: true}, whose result carries {type: 'terminal', terminalId}); bash_write {terminalId, input, newline?}; bash_output {terminalId, since?, wait?}; bash_kill {terminalId}; bash_resize {terminalId, cols, rows} (a terminal pane's resize of an interactive terminal's tty: integers, cols 20..500, rows 5..200; a non-interactive terminal answers not_a_tty); read {path, line?, limit?}; write {path, content, overwrite?}; glob {pattern, cwd?}; grep {pattern, path?, cwd?}. Unknown keys are refused.

AgentJobKind.description: The device-shell job kinds a first-party device may run on an agent computer.

AgentJobState.description: `queued_asleep`: the agent computer has no open poll; the job waits for its next poll inside the 600 s TTL. `expired`: the TTL ran out before a result.

AgentJobResult.description: Present once the state is `done` or `failed`.

AgentTerminalFrame.description: One `event: terminal` SSE frame. `output.seq` strictly increases; resume with `?since=<seq>`. The stream closes after `exit` or `gone`.

UsageReport.description: Usage in fixed-width UTC buckets, oldest first; empty buckets carry `results: []`.

webhook_secret.description: The signing secret for `webhook_url`, returned ONCE, here. Verify each delivery: `X-Superbot-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` where v1 is HMAC-SHA256(secret, `t + "." + body`).

CreatedRun.description: The run just started, plus its webhook secret when one was asked for.

RunBudget.description: What the run may spend: wall time, USD and legs.

status.description: `queued`, `running`, then one of `done`, `failed`, `needs_merge` (the work is on `branch` and waits for a merge) or `cancelled`.

source.description: What started the run. Runs started here are `api`.

project.description: The project the run works on.

prompt.description: The prompt, which is also the run’s title: show this to name the run. Null under zero data retention.

landing.description: `main` lands the work on the default branch; `pr` opens a pull request.

served_model.description: The model that served the run, as the runner reported it when the run settled (the same `served_model` the swarm reports). Null until then, and on a run that settled before this field existed.

served_lane.description: Who served the run’s model calls (the same `served_lane` the swarm reports). Every cloud run is `platform`: Superbot’s own model key, billed to the account’s wallet. Null on a run that predates this field.

branch.description: The branch the work sits on, when it did not land directly.

summary.description: The runner’s end-of-run diagnostic once it settles, a machine-readable line for debugging and for telling a failed run from a finished one (for example `done — sandbox fence-only, 127 tool call(s), local space sp_…`), and it can name internal ids. It is not a title and not the run’s answer: name the run by `prompt`, and do not show this text to end users. Null under zero data retention.

url.description: A deep link that opens the run’s project in the Superbot app (`superbot://project/<id>`), when the project id is linkable.

Run.description: One cloud agent run on a project.

first_id.description: Id of the first item on this page; pass as `before_id` for the previous page.

last_id.description: Id of the last item on this page; pass as `after_id` for the next page.

id.description: The project id to pass as `project` to createRun.

name.description: The project’s name in the Superbot app.

RunProjectList.description: Your projects linked to one repository: id and name only.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` on the next poll.

done.description: True once nothing more will happen to the run.

seq.description: Per-run sequence number; the SSE `id`, and what `after` / `Last-Event-ID` resume from.

note_id.description: On `note_queued` / `note_delivered`: the note’s id (never its text).

length.description: On `note_queued` / `note_delivered`: the note’s length in characters.

served_model.description: On `result` only: the model that served the run, as `served_model` on the run.

served_lane.description: On `result` only: who served the run, as `served_lane` on the run.

summary.description: On `result` only: the runner’s end-of-run diagnostic, as `summary` on the run (not a title or an answer). Null under zero data retention.

RunEvent.description: A status change, the settled result, the pull request a `pr` run opened, or a steering note queued on the run and then delivered to it.

RunNote.description: A note queued for a running run.

post.summary: Run a job on an agent computer
post.description: Queue one device-shell job on a linked agent computer, by its id. First-party only: a session or a device token of your own Superbot app; agent computer tokens, MCP connectors, caller keys and the account API key are refused (403). An asleep agent computer answers `queued_asleep`; the job waits for its next poll up to 600 s.

schema.description: An agent computer (`agt_…`) on your account.

parameters.description: An agent computer (`agt_…`) on your account.
parameters.name: device_id

get.description: The job and, once it is `done` or `failed`, its result. `wait` (seconds, at most 25) parks the read until the job settles. A job lost to a Superbot restart answers 410 `job_lost_in_restart` (`retryable: true`, `kind`): it may have run on the agent computer, so check before repeating anything that changes state, then send it again. An id nobody minted, another account's, or older than the 600 s job lifetime is 404 `job_not_found`.

410.description: Superbot restarted after the job was queued and its outcome was not kept (`job_lost_in_restart`, `retryable: true`, `kind`). Send the job again once a repeat is safe.

get.description: Server-sent events, every frame `event: terminal` with an AgentTerminalFrame as JSON: `output` (seq strictly increasing), then `exit` or `gone`, after which the stream closes. Resume with `since=<seq>` (or Last-Event-ID). Open a terminal with a `bash` job `{command: <login shell>, runInBackground: true, interactive: true}` (a real tty: prompts, sudo and TUIs work) and type into it with `bash_write`.

get.description: The team’s audit log, oldest first, as NDJSON (default) or CSV: who, on which device and through which agent, used which credential class for what, and the outcome. Rows are kept for a year. Owners and admins only; a member gets 403 and a caller outside the team 404. At most `limit` rows per request; when more remain, the `x-next-cursor` header carries the cursor for the next page. Columns, in CSV order: ts, org_id, actor_user_id, actor_email, device_id, agent, credential_class, credential_ref, action, target, outcome, request_id, ip, ua.
